standard.title: Intertextuality in literary texts
standard.description: identify intertextual references in literary texts and explain how the references enable new understanding of the aesthetic quality of the text
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify connections between texts and discuss how one text draws on or responds to another (AC9E7LE04). They have not yet examined intertextuality in literary texts specifically — how allusion or quotation in written texts enables new understanding of aesthetic quality through the meaning generated by the connection between texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify intertextual references in literary texts and explain how those references enable new understanding of the text's aesthetic quality.

nodes.label: Identifying literary intertextuality
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify an intertextual reference (allusion or quotation) in a literary text and explain what source it draws on.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one intertextual reference (allusion or direct quotation) in a literary text and name the source text it references.
nodes.typical_width: Identify intertextual references through allusion or quotation in written literary texts; explain how knowledge of the source text is required to understand the full meaning of the reference.
wider: Investigate how a literary text uses allusions to a specific cultural tradition (e.g. classical mythology, the Bible, a particular literary canon) and examine what knowledge that assumes of the reader
Examine how a contemporary author uses intertextual references to classic texts to position their work within a literary tradition
Compare how two authors allude to the same source text differently, examining what each achieves through the reference

response_modes.reason: Identifying an intertextual reference requires students to distinguish between a text simply mentioning something and deliberately alluding to it — a non-obvious interpretive move. Without explicit scaffolding of what constitutes an allusion and how to trace it to a source, students miss references or over-identify casual mentions as allusions.

success_criteria: Identifies a specific intertextual reference in a literary text.
Names the source text the reference draws on and explains what prior knowledge is needed to recognise it.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to explain how an intertextual reference enables new understanding of aesthetic quality — a task that is impossible if students cannot reliably identify references and name their source texts. Without solid identification at Node 1, Node 2 analysis is speculative rather than grounded.

nodes.label: Intertextuality and aesthetic quality
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how an intertextual reference in a literary text enables new understanding of the text's aesthetic quality — how the reference enriches the reader's appreciation of the text's meaning, craft or effect.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how one intertextual reference in a literary text adds to the reader's understanding or appreciation of the text's aesthetic quality — what the reference enables that a reading without knowledge of the source would miss.
nodes.typical_width: Identify intertextual references through allusion or quotation in literary texts and explain how knowledge of other texts influences the reader's understanding and appreciation of the aesthetic quality of the text being read.
wider: Analyse how sustained intertextual allusiveness (multiple references to a single source tradition) shapes the aesthetic identity of a literary text as a whole
Investigate how a parody or creative response to a canonical text generates aesthetic quality through the gap between the original and the imitation
Examine how a First Nations author's use of oral storytelling traditions as intertextual material creates aesthetic qualities not available within Western literary conventions alone

response_modes.reason: The connection between intertextual reference and aesthetic quality is abstract — students may understand that a reference exists without being able to articulate what it adds aesthetically. Explicit scaffolding of the 'what does this add that the text alone cannot provide?' question is needed to move from identification to aesthetic explanation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The relationship between intertextuality and aesthetic quality is genuinely sophisticated territory — examining how allusion to tradition, parody and creative reinterpretation each generate aesthetic meaning in different ways provides rich analytical depth for advancing students.
success_criteria: Explains how a specific intertextual reference enriches the reader's understanding or appreciation of a literary text.
Uses appropriate aesthetic vocabulary (e.g. 'layers of meaning', 'resonance', 'allusion', 'aesthetic effect') in the explanation.
